reasons: F01, F02: a material weakness in internal control over revenue is the strongest red flag on the card. Revenue is the area most often misstated.

F08, F09: revenue is mainly recognised over time and contract assets/unbilled receivables are significant. Revenue therefore depends on estimates (progress measurement), which makes the revenue control weakness worse.
F03: no auditor attestation on ICFR, so the reported weakness has not been independently tested and could be wider than disclosed.
F17: an active securities class action suggests investors may allege misleading disclosures.

F21, F22, R16, R07: a capital raise, securities issuance and a major acquisition happened in the same year, with leverage up sharply (LVGI 3.76). These raise financing pressure and the complexity of purchase accounting.
R17: the Dechow F-score of 1.26 is above the 1.0 threshold, and R13 soft assets of 0.76 point to a large share of judgement-dependent assets, probably acquisition goodwill and intangibles.
F26, F28: the emphasis on non-GAAP measures and a segment/reporting change reduce comparability and may divert attention from GAAP results.
Mitigating, R09, R08, R10: the Beneish M-score of -3.52 is well below the -1.78 threshold and accruals are negative (TATA -0.04, RSST -0.05), so accrual-based earnings management is not evident.

Mitigating, R01, R11, R18: DSRI 0.97 and receivables growing slower than sales give no sign of receivables being inflated. R19 CFO/NI of 13.21 means cash flow is far above net income, although net income is probably small.
Mitigating, F04, F05, F06, F07, F14, F15, F16: no going concern doubt, no auditor change, no disagreements, no prior-period correction, no executive turnover and no SEC inquiry.
